title: This week: G position, chords and rhythm

blocks.text: A week's work: a new hand position, the chords that go with it, rhythm and reading practice, and some songs. Do the parts in order, a part or two a day, and come back to the warm-up and rhythm steps every day. Every practice step keeps going as long as you like.

# Part 1. Warm-up: reading in C position, bass clef first
Most music gives the left hand fewer notes than the right, so the bass clef gets read less and stays slower. A few minutes a day fixes that. Your landmarks: **middle C** sits just above the bass staff (on its own short line); **bass C** is the second space up; and the **G on the bottom line** is where your left hand goes later this week.

The tunes in these steps are made up fresh for every card, so you read them instead of remembering them.

blocks.title: Unit 5: More Bass Clef Note Reading (Faber Piano Adventures, 5 min)

blocks.text: Start with single notes: one note a card, play it. A wrong key tells you which key you played and which note it was, with where it sits on the staff. 20 cards make a set; **Keep going** at the end deals more for as long as you like. A minute or two of these every day is the fastest way to read the bass clef as easily as the treble.

blocks.title: Single notes: bass clef
blocks.about: One note a card, every line and space of the bass staff. Play it.

blocks.title: Single notes: treble clef
blocks.about: One note a card, every line and space of the treble staff. Play it.

blocks.text: Now short tunes in C position, made up fresh for every card. The blue note is the one to play next; notes you have played turn green. **Hear it** plays the card with every note's letter written under it (the letters go when you start playing).

blocks.title: Bass clef, C position
blocks.about: Read each short tune and play it with your left hand in C position. No clock: play each note when you have read it.

blocks.text: Then the same in time. One bar of clicks counts you in; after that the click keeps going and the cards keep coming, one in the treble clef and one in the bass at random, with a bar between them to look at the next one (it's shown faded underneath while you play). Each note gets a dot as you play it: green on time, orange early or late, red for a wrong key. Start at 60; use **+** when it feels easy.

blocks.title: Both clefs, C position, in time
blocks.about: Read and play in time with the click, card after card. Stop when you like.

blocks.text:
# Part 2. G position
The same shape as C position, moved: the right hand up so its thumb is on G, the left hand down so its little finger is on G.

blocks.title: Unit 9: G Pentascales (Faber Piano Adventures, 4 min)
blocks.text:
**Right hand:** thumb (1) on the G above middle C, then fingers 2, 3, 4, 5 on A, B, C and D. On the treble staff that G is the second line up; the five notes run line, space, line, space, line, up to the D on the fourth line.

**Left hand:** little finger (5) on the G two below middle C, then 4, 3, 2, 1 on A, B, C and D. On the bass staff that G is the bottom line; the five notes run up to the D on the middle line.

Everything you do in C position carries over: curved fingers, one finger to a key, and the hand moves as a whole when it moves to a new position. None of the five notes needs a black key.

blocks.caption: Try the right hand: switch between finger numbers and key names.

blocks.title: G position, right hand
blocks.about: Read each tune in the treble clef and play it in G position. No clock.

blocks.title: G position, left hand
blocks.about: Read each tune in the bass clef (bottom line to middle line) and play it in G position. No clock.

blocks.title: G position, in time
blocks.about: G position in either hand, in time with the click, card after card.

blocks.title: Intervals: 2nds and 3rds, bass clef
blocks.about: Two notes a card, a step or a skip apart, up or down. Play both.

blocks.title: Intervals: 2nds and 3rds, treble clef
blocks.about: The same in the treble clef.

blocks.title: Intervals: 4ths and 5ths
blocks.about: Bigger gaps: a 4th line to space (or space to line), a 5th line to the line two up (or space to the space two up).

blocks.text:
# Part 3. Rhythm
Ten minutes a day. This screen works like a rhythm trainer: one bar counts in, then exercises keep coming on a click that doesn't stop. Tap the big pad (or any key) for each note. Every tap gets a dot over its note: **green** on time, **orange** early (←) or late (→), **grey** missed, and a grey tick for a tap where there's no note. Under the music: how that exercise went; at the top, your share on time and how many in a row.

- **Tap along** plays the rhythm with you; **Read** gives you only the click. Start a level with Tap along if it's new, then switch to Read: reading it is the skill.
- **− / +** change the tempo; **Speed up by itself** adds 5 after three good exercises in a row.
- **Loop this one** repeats the exercise you're on until you switch it off.
- **Judge note lengths** also marks a note let go too soon (off unless you want it).
- Count in your head, *1 2 3 4*. A round is 8 exercises; stop whenever you like, or just stop tapping.

blocks.title: Rhythm 1: quarters, halves, wholes and rests
blocks.about: Tap each note in time. Rests: stay still and keep counting.

blocks.title: Rhythm 2: dotted halves and 3/4
blocks.about: A dotted half lasts three beats; in 3/4 a bar has three.

blocks.title: Rhythm 3: eighth notes
blocks.about: Two eighths share a beat: count "1 and 2 and".

blocks.title: Rhythm 4: everything, 3/4 and 4/4
blocks.about: All of it mixed, both time signatures.

blocks.text:
# Part 4. Chords
You know three chords in C with your left hand. In G the same three jobs are done by G, C and D7, played from G position.

blocks.title: Unit 16: Primary Chords in G Major (Faber Piano Adventures, 4 min)
blocks.text:
**In C (review):** C is C–E–G (fingers 5 3 1). F is C–F–A (5 2 1). G7 is B–F–G (5 2 1).

**In G:** **G** is G–B–D (5 3 1), the left hand's G position with fingers 5, 3 and 1. **C** is G–C–E (5 2 1): the little finger stays on G, 2 moves up to C, and the thumb reaches up to E. **D7** is F♯–C–D (5 2 1).

**The ♯ (sharp):** it means the black key just above. F♯ is the black key just to the right of F. A sharp written in a bar counts for the rest of that bar.

Why these three? Each key has a **home** chord (C in C, G in G), a chord that **leans away** (F in C, C in G) and one that **pulls back home** (G7 in C, D7 in G). Notice the pattern: the home chord's notes in G position are the same finger shape as C in C position. Many simple songs need only these three.

blocks.title: Chords in C, by name
blocks.about: A name comes up (C, F or G7): play that chord with your left hand, all three notes together.

blocks.title: Chords in G, by name
blocks.about: A name comes up (G, C or D7): play that chord with your left hand, all three notes together.

blocks.text: Now change chords on the beat. Each card is four bars, one chord a bar, written on the bass staff; it counts in a bar of clicks, then play each chord on beat 1 and hold it through the bar. Get your hand to the next chord during the last beat, not after the click.

blocks.title: Changing chords in time
blocks.about: One chord a bar, on beat 1, held for the whole bar. In C and in G.

blocks.text: One more chord, and the best-known four chords in pop: **C – G – Am – F**. **Am** (A minor) is A–C–E; with your left hand in C position, play C–E and move your thumb up to A, or play A–C–E with fingers 5 3 1 from the A below. A great many 2000s songs run on these four chords, in this order or close to it. The band plays along; you play the chords on beat 1 of each bar.

blocks.caption: Am from C position: C and E, thumb up to A

blocks.title: Four chords with the band
blocks.about: Play C, G, Am, F on beat 1 of each bar with the band. Keep going as long as you like.

blocks.text:
# Part 5. Songs
Each song opens in **Wait for me**: the music waits for your right notes, so take it as slowly as you need. When it goes smoothly, switch the mode to **Play along** and play it in time (start slow with −). Right hand first, then left, then together.

## C review: Chasing Cars
*Snow Patrol, 2006.* The chorus, moved to C so it sits in C position: the right hand only ever plays C, D, E and F (fingers 1 to 4), over the chords you know, C, G7 and F, one a bar. Each phrase starts before the bar line: two quick notes and a longer one on beats 3 and 4, then a long note on beat 1. Learn it in Wait for me, then Play along slowly; the record is at 104.

blocks.title: Chasing Cars
blocks.about: Melody with your right hand in C position, one chord a bar with your left.

blocks.text:
## Ode to Joy in G
You know this tune. Now in G position, with G and D7 under it.

blocks.title: Ode to Joy in G
blocks.about: Right hand in G position, left hand G and D7.

blocks.text:
## When the Saints Go Marching In
All three G chords: G, C and D7. The right hand never leaves G position.

blocks.title: When the Saints Go Marching In
blocks.about: Right hand in G position; left hand G, C and D7.

blocks.text:
## Seven Nation Army
*The White Stripes, 2003.* The riff, in your left hand, low in the bass clef: **E E G E D C B**. Fingers: B 5, C 4, D 3, E 2, G 1 (no finger on F). Learn the notes in Wait for me, then switch to Play along at a slow tempo: the rhythm is the fun part. A long E, a short E, G on beat 3, then E and D just off the beat, and two long notes, C and B.

blocks.title: Seven Nation Army
blocks.about: The riff in your left hand. Notes first (Wait for me), then in time.

blocks.text:
## A stretch (optional): Someone You Loved
*Lewis Capaldi, 2019.* A melody with eighth notes over the four chords from Part 4 (C, G, Am, F). It's a stretch: it moves around more than this week's songs. Learn the right hand in Wait for me at a slow tempo, a few bars at a time; the intro (the first four bars) is the hardest part, so you can start at bar 5.

blocks.title: Someone You Loved
blocks.about: Right hand first, slowly. A stretch, for when the rest is going well.

blocks.text:
# To finish
Keep the warm-up and a rhythm level as a daily habit. Next week: more songs in G, and the G major scale.
